newsitem.title: UK: CBI says BOE should leave UK rate alone for now.
newsitem.headline: CBI says BOE should leave UK rate alone for now.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Thursday that the Bank of England's new monetary policy committee, which sets interest rates, faced a very dificult decision this week but on balance rates should be left on hold for now.

"Interest rates can be left on hold for the moment, firstly because we want to see the budget, and secondly because a rise could push the pound still higher," said Sudhir Junankar, associate director of economic analysis.
The MPC starts its inaugural two day meeting at 1400 GMT on Thursday.
The CBI expects modest personal tax rises of 2-3 billion pounds in Brown's first budget, due to be delivered on July 2.
He said the British economy was showing signs of strong economic growth in some area but the recovery is slightly unbalanced. "It leaves the MPC with a very difficult decision."
The key news from the CBI's latest survey was that price pressures remain weak on the high street.
"That weakness was a considerable surprise to us...it is more to do with domestic competition than lower input prices," Junankar said.
The CBI distributive trades survey showed lower sales growth but that was highly localised with most sectors performing strongly.
Motor traders, who are not included in the survey sample, saw sales volume rise in May despite expectations of a decline.
Wholesale volumes picked up further in May, increasing at the faster annual rate since November last year.
